pathwayAssessments.assessment: Retain nasal retinal crossing, LGN/optic-radiation/V1 route and retinotopy; parallel pretectal/collicular routes and variable field defects remain qualified.
refs: Blumenfeld, Neuroanatomy through Clinical Cases, 2nd ed. (2010), pp. 463-476 (PDF pp. 489-502), Figures 11.6-11.8 and 11.15

pathwayAssessments.assessment: Retain cochlear relays through SOC/lateral lemniscus/IC/MGN to auditory cortex. Bilateral projections and non-obligatory SOC passage are explicit; this is a composite route.
refs: Blumenfeld, 2nd ed., pp. 519-522 (PDF pp. 545-548), Figures 12.16-12.17

pathwayAssessments.assessment: Retain preferential entorhinal layer II to dentate/CA3 and layer III to CA1/subiculum, mossy fibres and Schaffer collaterals. The trisynaptic teaching loop is not the whole recurrent network.
refs: Blumenfeld, 2nd ed., pp. 834-837 (PDF pp. 860-863), Figures 18.8, 18.11 and 18.13

Witter MP, Amaral DG (1991). Entorhinal cortex of the monkey: V. Projections to dentate gyrus, hippocampus, and subicular complex. J Comp Neurol 307:437-459. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1713237/ (primary macaque tracing; layer contributions are preferential, not exclusive)

pathwayAssessments.assessment: Retain hippocampal/subicular output through fornix, mammillary bodies, mammillothalamic tract, anterior thalamus and cingulate/entorhinal return. The loop is not a complete memory or emotion system.
refs: Blumenfeld, 2nd ed., pp. 834-837 (PDF pp. 860-863), Figures 18.8, 18.11 and 18.13

pathwayAssessments.assessment: Retain net disinhibition via striatum to GPi/SNr and thalamocortical output in the simplified direct model; inhibitory signs and dopamine qualifications agree with the textbook.
refs: Blumenfeld, 2nd ed., pp. 748-752 (PDF pp. 774-778), Figures 16.5-16.8; textbook explicitly describes direct/indirect model as incomplete

pathwayAssessments.assessment: Retain striatum-GPe-STN-GPi/SNr sign relationships and simplified net inhibition of thalamic output. Parallel, recurrent and cell-population limitations remain explicit.
refs: Blumenfeld, 2nd ed., pp. 748-752 (PDF pp. 774-778), Figures 16.5-16.8; textbook explicitly describes direct/indirect model as incomplete

pathwayAssessments.assessment: Correct the linked arcuate step to dorsal connections only; retain distributed reciprocal language networks and the separate, unmodeled ventral contribution.
refs: Blumenfeld, 2nd ed., pp. 885-887 and 894-897 (PDF pp. 911-913 and 920-923), Figure 19.2; language processing involves distributed reciprocal networks

pathwayAssessments.assessment: Retain cortex/capsule/crus/pontine/pyramid route and predominantly crossed lateral CST. The anterior CST and fine somatotopy are not represented as complete geometry.
refs: Blumenfeld, Neuroanatomy through Clinical Cases, 2nd ed. (2010), Ch. 6, pp. 231-242, Figures 6.8-6.11

pathwayAssessments.assessment: Retain predominantly bilateral inputs with contralateral lower-facial and tongue emphasis; motor-nucleus specificity and distinction from the travelling corticospinal fibres are qualified.
refs: Blumenfeld, Neuroanatomy through Clinical Cases, 2nd ed. (2010), Ch. 12, pp. 512-514, 535-538, Figure 12.7 and clinical concepts

pathwayAssessments.assessment: Retain ipsilateral dorsal-column ascent to gracile/cuneate nuclei, caudal-medullary sensory crossing, medial lemniscus, VPL and somatosensory cortex.
refs: Blumenfeld, Neuroanatomy through Clinical Cases, 2nd ed. (2010), Ch. 7, pp. 277-280, Figures 7.1 and 7.3

pathwayAssessments.assessment: Retain dorsal-horn relay, short segmental crossing and contralateral ascending pain/temperature route. Bilateral and additional anterolateral projections remain qualified.
refs: Blumenfeld, Neuroanatomy through Clinical Cases, 2nd ed. (2010), Ch. 7, pp. 278-282, Figures 7.2 and 7.4

pathwayAssessments.assessment: Retain distinct principal and spinal trigeminal sensory relays, predominantly crossed VPM projection and bilateral components; a single curve does not represent every modality branch.
refs: Blumenfeld, Neuroanatomy through Clinical Cases, 2nd ed. (2010), Ch. 12, pp. 509-512, Figure 12.8

pathwayAssessments.assessment: Retain vestibular-to-abducens and crossed internuclear MLF-to-oculomotor relationships for conjugate horizontal gaze; vestibular and vertical pathways extend beyond this example.
refs: Blumenfeld, Neuroanatomy through Clinical Cases, 2nd ed. (2010), Ch. 12, pp. 523-525, Figure 12.19
Blumenfeld, Neuroanatomy through Clinical Cases, 2nd ed. (2010), Ch. 13, pp. 584-587, Figure 13.13

pathwayAssessments.assessment: Retain ipsilateral cortical input to pontine nuclei and crossed pontocerebellar input via the MCP; cerebellar cortex/deep output relations remain schematic.
refs: Blumenfeld, Neuroanatomy through Clinical Cases, 2nd ed. (2010), Ch. 15, pp. 704-710, Figures 15.9-15.10

pathwayAssessments.assessment: Retain dorsal/cuneocerebellar mainly ipsilateral inputs and the ventral route double-crossing qualification. The known incorrect anterior tract geometry remains withheld.
refs: Blumenfeld, Neuroanatomy through Clinical Cases, 2nd ed. (2010), Ch. 15, pp. 708-711, Table 15.3 and Figure 15.11

pathwayAssessments.assessment: Retain major deep-nuclear output through crossed SCP to thalamic/red-nuclear targets, with fastigial/vestibular exceptions. Not every cerebellothalamic fibre relays in the red nucleus.
refs: Blumenfeld, Neuroanatomy through Clinical Cases, 2nd ed. (2010), Ch. 15, pp. 704-708, Figures 15.9A-C

pathwayAssessments.assessment: Retain cortical-STN-GPi/SNr fast excitatory route as a teaching example grounded in primary primate physiology. Species and incomplete human behavioural-model limits remain explicit.
refs: Nambu et al. (2000), Excitatory cortical inputs to pallidal neurons via the subthalamic nucleus in the monkey, J Neurophysiol 84:289-300, https://doi.org/10.1152/jn.2000.84.1.289 (primary primate physiology; not a full model of human behavior)
Blumenfeld, Neuroanatomy through Clinical Cases, 2nd ed. (2010), Ch. 16, pp. 748-752 (context and limitations of direct/indirect model)

pathwayAssessments.assessment: Retain three-neuron hypothalamic/spinal/SCG route with carotid-associated ocular fibres; Horner signs and sweat distribution depend on lesion level.
refs: Blumenfeld, Neuroanatomy through Clinical Cases, 2nd ed. (2010), Ch. 13, pp. 578-581, Figure 13.10

pathwayAssessments.assessment: Retain IX/X visceral afferents to NTS and parasympathetic motor relays; baroreflex and organ-specific outputs are examples of a larger distributed autonomic network.
refs: Blumenfeld, Neuroanatomy through Clinical Cases, 2nd ed. (2010), Ch. 12, pp. 530-535, Figures 12.22-12.23

findings.title: SLF search alias equates a related component with the entire system
findings.explanation: Arcuate naming varies among classifications, but even a scheme grouping it within the SLF distinguishes it as one component. The atlas has a separate arcuate record; remove the whole-system identity alias while preserving the naming-convention caveat.

findings.title: Language route labels both dorsal and ventral connections as arcuate

targets.original: Arcuate/SLF-related dorsal routes support auditory-motor integration and repetition; additional temporal-frontal routes support comprehension. Arcuate fasciculus is not identical to the entire SLF.
targets.proposed: Arcuate/SLF-related dorsal routes contribute to auditory-motor integration and repetition. Parallel ventral temporal-frontal connections also contribute to comprehension and are not represented by the arcuate link. Naming conventions vary; the arcuate is not the entire SLF.

findings.explanation: The clickable relay is the arcuate fasciculus. A dual-stream title implied it represented ventral connections too. Narrow the title and retain the distributed network and unmodeled ventral route.

findings.title: Auditory tonotopy claim is more absolute than the detailed card

targets.original: Special sensory — audition, tonotopically organized at every relay
targets.proposed: Special sensory — audition, with tonotopic organization at major relays; frequency gradients vary between subnuclei

findings.explanation: The textbook teaches tonotopy throughout the principal auditory route. Human high-field fMRI identifies subdivision-dependent gradients; the existing somatotopy paragraph already qualifies the composite curve. Harmonize the short modality label without asserting loss of principal-pathway tonotopy.

findings.title: Spinoreticular origin excludes experimentally demonstrated dorsal-horn contributions

targets.original: Projection neurons distributed in spinal intermediate-zone/ventral-horn laminae VI-VIII, within the broader anterolateral system.
targets.proposed: Spinal projection neurons in dorsal-horn, intermediate-zone and ventral-horn regions. Primate tracing identifies prominent lamina VII-VIII contributions and additional dorsal-horn neurons; a fixed human laminar census is not implied.

findings.explanation: Figure 7.2 places the composite input in spinal sensory circuitry. Primary monkey tracing found prominent VII-VIII neurons and dorsal-horn contributions, especially V. Retain the broad nociception/arousal circuit but remove the VI-VIII-only distribution.

findings.title: Sensory-decusssation plate draws a pre-crossing lateral corticospinal bundle

targets.original: Two lateral ellipses and a lateral corticospinal label in the sensory-decusssation section
targets.proposed: Remove these ellipses/label; retain the ventral pyramid representing pre-crossing corticospinal fibers
Remove tract-corticospinal-lateral from this plate manifest

findings.explanation: The sensory crossing is rostral to the pyramidal decussation. At the illustrated caudal-medullary sensory level, corticospinal fibers remain in ventral pyramids; a separate already-crossed lateral bundle is misleading.

targets.original: Two internal-arcuate crossing paths and label in the motor-decusssation section
targets.proposed: Remove the sensory crossing paths and label from this motor crossing plate
Remove tract-internal-arcuate from this plate manifest

findings.explanation: The textbook explicitly illustrates these crossings at different rostrocaudal levels. Removing the sensory crossing from the motor-crossing plate preserves the teaching distinction; nearby dorsal nuclei remain approximate schematic context.

findings.title: Authored sections combine levels and contain stale context captions

targets.original: No specific composite-section notice next to author plate
targets.proposed: Authored teaching schematic: nearby anatomical levels may be combined. Shapes, boundaries and marker positions are approximate; this is not a validated single anatomical section.

targets.original: Dashed gray strokes are untagged context: lateral ventricle and uncus/hippocampal edge (no registry records).
targets.proposed: Dashed gray strokes show ventricular and medial temporal context; their contours are schematic.

targets.original: Dashed gray strokes are untagged context: optic tract toward the LGN (no registry record for the optic tract).
targets.proposed: Dashed gray strokes show optic-pathway context toward the LGN; no additional selectable contour is defined here.

findings.explanation: Diencephalic and coronal diagrams combine structures distributed across serial levels. Book sections support their broad relationships, not strict coplanarity. A specific in-view notice prevents this implication; old no-registry-record captions no longer match the current dataset.
